snippets.doc: Version of Java when the the product was implemented.
snippets.label: @since

snippets.doc: Documents a value parameter of a function or a type parameter of a class, property or function. To better separate the parameter name from the description, if you prefer, you can enclose the name of the parameter in brackets. This is a synonym of @param.
snippets.label: @parameter

snippets.doc: A Kotlin comment block including short summary, description, param, return, and example.
snippets.label: comment

snippets.doc: The @deprecated description in the first sentence should at least tell the user when the API was deprecated and what to use as a replacement. Only the first sentence will appear in the summary section and index. Subsequent sentences can also explain why it has been deprecated.
snippets.label: @Deprecated

snippets.doc: Documents the primary constructor of a class.
snippets.label: @constructor

snippets.doc: A simple Kotlin comment block with short summary and description. Useful when the user prefers to manually add the other documentation tags.
snippets.label: comment_simple

snippets.doc: Documents the receiver of an extension function.
snippets.label: @receiver

snippets.doc: Documents a value parameter of a function or a type parameter of a class, property or function. To better separate the parameter name from the description, if you prefer, you can enclose the name of the parameter in brackets. This is a synonym of @parameter.
snippets.label: @param

snippets.doc: Documents the property of a class which has the specified name. This tag can be used for documenting properties declared in the primary constructor, where putting a doc comment directly before the property definition would be awkward.
snippets.label: @property

snippets.doc: Embeds the body of the function with the specified qualified name into the documentation for the current element, in order to show an example of how the element could be used.
snippets.label: @sample

snippets.doc: References another item or piece of documentation.
snippets.label: @see

snippets.doc: You can provide one @author tag, multiple @author tags, or no @author tags. For classes and interfaces only, required.
snippets.label: @author

snippets.doc: Documents an exception which can be thrown by a method. Since Kotlin does not have checked exceptions, there is also no expectation that all possible exceptions are documented, but you can still use this tag when it provides useful information for users of the class. Synonym of @exception.
snippets.label: @throws

snippets.doc: Excludes the element from the generated documentation. Can be used for elements which are not part of the official API of a module but still have to be visible externally.
snippets.label: @suppress

snippets.doc: Documents an exception which can be thrown by a method. Since Kotlin does not have checked exceptions, there is also no expectation that all possible exceptions are documented, but you can still use this tag when it provides useful information for users of the class. Synonym of @throws.
snippets.label: @exception

snippets.doc: While there is no dedicated tag for examples on Kotlin, we can still include them as plain text. This allows you illustrate the usage or behavior of a particular code element.
snippets.label: example

snippets.doc: Adds an example to the documentation.
snippets.label: @example
